title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཧ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 108)
shelf_note: A Madhyamaka commentary in the Derge woodblock (sūtra-citing commentary on conventional vs ultimate truth, the selflessness of phenomena and the yogin's fearlessness). It belongs in the dbu ma section of the Tengyur.

ocr_errors.problem: The OCR puts a variant-reading brace into the transcription. The print shows one reading (ཆུང་ཟད). Otherwise all 8 lines match the block, from 'ཅད་ལ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བ' to '།མཐོང'.

tr_errors_A.english: then those seeking the path would be discouraged
tr_errors_A.problem: ཉམས means the search would be ruined or pointless. It does not mean the seekers would be psychologically discouraged. A also drops the ཞེ་ན objection marker from this sentence, and only the following 'To address this' signals it.

tr_errors_A.english: the effort ... would be exhausted and fruitless; that is the meaning of being discouraged
tr_errors_A.problem: ངལ་བ ('toil') is turned into 'exhausted', and the gloss of ཉམས is again given as 'discouraged'. The point is that the toil would be fruitless and therefore 'ruined'.

tr_errors_A.english: <insert>slight</insert> <gloss>original: chung zad</gloss> <note>the text notes an alternative reading ...</note>
tr_errors_A.problem: The note says the text itself notes an alternative reading. The variant comes from the OCR brace, not from the print. The reader also sees an unknown <insert> tag and a cluttered run of three tags.

tr_errors_B.english: wishing to abandon suffering through this path
tr_errors_B.problem: B supplies 'suffering' as the object of སྤང་བ. The object is implicit in the source, and B's choice is defensible from the preceding clause.

other.note: The A text uses a non-standard <insert> tag that the reader format may not render.

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error. B renders ཉམས ('ruined') and ངལ་བ ('toil') correctly and keeps the objection-reply structure explicit, while A twice turns ཉམས into 'discouraged' and adds a note about a textual variant that is not on the print.

book_verdict: The print matches the transcription almost word for word, and both translations follow the argument faithfully. B is cleaner; A has two moderate lexical slips about the 'ruined' path and a cluttered variant note.
